transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-26
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (CTO - Beacon Health), Lina Cho (ML Eng), Meera Singh (Product)

Summary: quick review of last week's benchmark runs, discuss pinning to specific model versions in the Redwood catalog, talk through rollback/fallback mechanics and a plan for canary.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick availability check, looks like we have everyone. Carlos, you good?
[00:07] Carlos Ramirez: Yeah good, thanks Maya. Lina, Meera here.
[00:11] Maya Patel: Great. Jordan and I, we'll kick off with the benchmark recap and then hand off to Lina for any questions from engineering.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Cool. So recapping the runs we did Monday — we ran the same prompt set you provided, 500 eval prompts, sequence len averaged ~128 tokens, we tested Redwood-70B (float) and rw-13b-q4 and rw-13b-8bit variants.
[00:38] Jordan Lee: High-level, Redwood-70B gives the best quality on the clinical summarization subset but its latency is high on your dedicated 4-GPU pool — p95s ~560ms with batch size 4, cost roughly 2.7x over rw-13b-q4.
[00:54] Carlos Ramirez: Right, that's expected. Our main constraint is user-facing latency, target p95 under 300ms. If 70B is twice the cost and almost double the latency we might not be able to accept it for the first rollout.
[01:10] Lina Cho: Can you share exact config? GPU type, batching, seq len? I saw some differences in the run sheet.
[01:16] Jordan Lee: Yeah — we used A100s on the Dedicated pool you're running, batch size 4, concurrency 16 in the test harness, KV cache warm for repeated prefixes. Sequence length 128 average but there were outliers to 512. I'll drop the exact config in the spreadsheet.
[01:32] Meera Singh: Is the KV cache behaving as expected? We noticed some odd token cost variance last week.
[01:38] Jordan Lee: Worth noting transcription — sorry, I mean the KV cache, sometimes shows up as 'K-V cash' in the logs, haha, auto-transcribe — but cache hits were stable at ~72% for the test set, that helped the rw-13b variants.
[01:52] Maya Patel: Okay, so action point — Jordan will share the spreadsheet and the run configs.

[02:05] Jordan Lee: On pinning: we recommend pinning the POC to rw-13b-q4 for initial canary because it meets your latency target at p95 ~220–240ms with batch size 4 and concurrency tuned. Quality drop vs 70B is measurable on edge clinical cases but within your tolerance if we mitigate with a fallback.
[02:28] Carlos Ramirez: Fallback meaning what? If the response seems low-confidence, we call 70B? That would blow cost though.
[02:35] Jordan Lee: Two-tier fallback: primary is rw-13b-q4; for flagged prompts (high complexity or low confidence per the scoring function) route to Redwood-70B but only for a sampled percent or asynchronous re-rank. Alternatively, you can do a synchronous fallback but with rate limits to cap spend. We can also keep a cheap reranker model (rw-7b or an embedding similarity) to decide when to escalate.
[02:58] Lina Cho: Technical question — does the platform allow automatic fallback with a canary threshold and automatic rollback if error rates spike?
[03:06] Maya Patel: Yes — our routing policies support canary rules and thresholds. If error rate or latency crosses a configured SLO, you can auto-rollback to the previous model or redirect to a lower-cost variant. Jordan, correct if I'm misrepresenting.
[03:18] Jordan Lee: Correct. Policies can be time-windowed and tied to metrics (latency p95, error rate, model mismatch in quality checks). We also support A/B style rollouts and gradual traffic shifting.

[03:34] Carlos Ramirez: I want to avoid surprise costs. How do we estimate the unit economics for a fallback that hits 10% of requests to 70B?
[03:42] Jordan Lee: In your spreadsheet I will include per-token cost estimates for each model and a scenario calc. Rough ballpark: if rw-13b-q4 cost unit is X, 70B is ~2.5–3X. So a 10% fallback increases total spend by roughly 10% * (2.5–1) = 15% on top of baseline, plus possible request overhead. We'll give concrete numbers.
[04:02] Meera Singh: For quality measurement, we want a small set of canary prompts that always run on both models for comparison — value: continuous regression detection. Can we pin those?
[04:12] Jordan Lee: Absolutely, you can configure a fixed evaluation slice that duplicates a sample to both models for logging and quality metrics. This is what our Optimize product hooks into for regression alerts.

[04:28] Lina Cho: About pinning versions — our concern is that the catalog updates and a model can be replaced in-place. How do we ensure the POC sticks to the exact model binary?
[04:37] Maya Patel: Good point. Redwood has model-version pinning. You can pin to a model-version hash or explicit tag like "rw-13b-q4@v2025-05-20". By default catalog references can map to newer builds, but pinning locks you to the specific artifact.
[04:52] Carlos Ramirez: If we pin and later find a regression, what's the rollback path?
[04:56] Jordan Lee: Rollback is straightforward — change the route to the previous pinned version or to an alternative model. For automated rollback, you can set thresholds to revert traffic if metrics degrade. The control plane keeps previous versions for a retention period so you can switch back.

[05:14] Meera Singh: Any gotchas with quantized variants? We saw some hallucination in a small set when using q4.
[05:21] Jordan Lee: Quantization can change numeric stability for some architectures, and certain prompts with long-range dependencies can shift outputs. Our recommended approach is to keep an evaluation set during the POC and sample real user prompts to check for distribution shift. If hallucinations appear, you can either bump to an fp16 variant for those cases or use targeted prompt engineering/fallback rules.

[05:43] Lina Cho: On the security front — our legal team asked about KMS integration and whether keys are stored in Redwood or customer-managed.
[05:50] Maya Patel: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; for Dedicated we can integrate with cloud KMS with BYOK options. I'll send the SOC2 and KMS docs in the follow-up.
[06:03] Carlos Ramirez: Good. Also VPC peering vs Private option — the data residency questions were about logs. Can we redact or control retention?
[06:11] Jordan Lee: Yes, retention and audit log controls are configurable. For Private you control log storage. For Dedicated, we have retention policies and can mask PII in logs on ingest if required.

[06:27] Maya Patel: Quick demo note — last week we observed the rw-13b-q4 was closer to your latency SLO; if you want we can run a microbenchmark with your 90th percentile seq len and 1k concurrent requests to simulate peak. Lina?
[06:39] Lina Cho: Yes please, that would be helpful. Also, please include the exact sequence length distribution — when we tested earlier our tails spiked to 1k tokens which changed the picture.
[06:50] Jordan Lee: We'll add distribution and a run with p99 tail emphasis. Also we'll test with different batching configs — sometimes smaller batches at higher concurrency yield better p95.

[07:05] Carlos Ramirez: About monitoring — are there pre-built dashboards for per-model token costs and per-route latency?
[07:11] Maya Patel: Yep, Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and trace hooks. We'll share a link to a sample dashboard and the json for your Grafana if you want to ingest metrics.
[07:23] Meera Singh: For the canary, can we do a 5% traffic shift for 24 hours, check quality and cost, then expand?
[07:28] Jordan Lee: That's a standard pattern. We can also do a duplication of 1% traffic to the candidate model for offline eval.

[07:41] Lina Cho: One more technical — model compatibility: can the routing layer do auto-fallback to a smaller model architecture if the primary model's runtime is overloaded? Like switching from 13B to 7B automatically?
[07:50] Jordan Lee: Yes — routing policies can route to compatible variants by tag (e.g., semantic equivalence). You define compatibility lists and fallback weights; the system can shift traffic to a lower-cost variant if latency breaks.

[08:04] Maya Patel: Let's capture the next steps: Jordan will share the spreadsheet with full configs; Lina will run the 1k sample microbench; Maya will send security docs. Also we set a tentative canary date.

[08:18] Carlos Ramirez: Sounds good. Anything else?
[08:22] Meera Singh: No, that's it from Product — thanks.

[08:26] Maya Patel: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifacts.

-- End of recorded transcript --

Notes on transcription: occasional auto-transcribe errors (K-V cache spelled differently), speaker labels sometimes generic, natural fillers preserved.
